issues.detail: The Hebrew 'מִקֶּרֶב חוקך' means 'from the midst of your bosom/chest' (i.e., from within Your bosom), but the Vietnamese says 'khỏi lòng Ngài' (from Your heart), which is a different body part. The Hebrew 'חוקך' is 'bosom/chest', not 'heart' (לֵב). This changes the imagery and meaning.

The Vietnamese adds 'kẻ thù' (the enemy) which is not present in the Hebrew. The Hebrew 'כַלֵּה' means 'consume/destroy' without specifying the object; the object is implied from context (likely 'them' referring to enemies), but the explicit addition of 'kẻ thù' is an addition not in the Hebrew text.
